Subject: Scheduling: APAC demo — timezone matrix & avoid next-day rollover

Hi Kenji / Maya / Liam,

Thanks again for the interest — excited to show a short 30–40min walkthrough of Redwood inference for your storefront use case. I want to avoid the common calendar confusion where a single invite shows as “next day” for one office and “same day” for another, which caused last-minute no-shows elsewhere.

Quick proposal: I can do one of these windows (all times shown with JST / SGT / AEST annotations):
- Option A: 15:00 JST / 14:00 SGT / 16:00 AEST (30–40m)
- Option B: 09:30 JST / 08:30 SGT / 10:30 AEST (30–40m)
- Option C: 18:00 JST / 17:00 SGT / 19:00 AEST (shorter; 25m)

If any of those push a participant into the next calendar day locally (e.g., late-night), call that out and we can create separate invites for JP vs AU/SG to avoid ICS rollovers. I attached a tiny timezone matrix (apac-timezone-matrix.csv) and included two .ics variants in case you prefer a specific timezone anchor.

Please reply with preferred option and who needs the PST/UTC anchor (for your APAC -> EMEA handoffs). If helpful, Ava and Soojin are on copy to confirm calendar limits and to send calendar invites pinned to a timezone.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Marcus — thanks, appreciate showing options. Quick clarifications from our side:
- Tokyo team prefers early afternoon local time (13:00–15:30 JST).
- Singapore team (Maya) is fine during 10:00–16:00 SGT but we need to avoid anything that appears as a different calendar date for our Sydney office (Liam) because they run day-of-week reports tied to calendar date boundaries.

Practical ask: can you explicitly state the UTC anchor in the invite? For example, if we pick your Option A as 15:00 JST, please put that as 06:00 UTC in the event description. That helps our scheduling automation. Also, Liam — can you confirm whether DST is in effect the week of the 22nd? (We operate under AEDT sometimes).

On another note — the .ics file I imported yesterday from a different vendor wound up showing the event as Nov 10 in their system even though the UTC time was the same; we don't want that surprise.
